law_name: Programme of the 21st Government of the Republic of Lithuania (Seimas resolution approving the government programme)
description: Presented to the Seimas by Sinkevičius on 7 July and approved on 14 July 2026 by 72 votes to 29, with four abstentions, giving his cabinet its powers. It names polarisation, Russia's war against Ukraine, demographic decline and rising living costs among the main challenges, and pledges defence funding meeting the armed forces' needs, an air- and drone-defence system, higher pensions and incomes, a family-support overhaul, progressive taxation for top earners, a temporary halt to diesel excise increases, normalised relations with China and full CERN membership.
significance: Basis for the verdicts in this profile's promises. Its submission procedure is before the Constitutional Court, which on 16 September 2026 accepted an opposition petition arguing that it was registered before the cabinet was appointed.

law_name: Draft 2027–2029 state budget (2027 m. valstybės biudžeto ir savivaldybių biudžetų finansinių rodiklių patvirtinimo įstatymo projektas)
description: Approved by the government on 16 October 2026 and submitted to the Seimas: revenue of €22.2 billion and expenditure of €27.9 billion in 2027, a projected general government deficit of 3.8% of GDP and debt of 48.2% of GDP. It allocates €4.8 billion (5% of GDP) to defence, €715.5 million more for pensions (average old-age pension +10.4%), €450.2 million for public-sector pay rises (about 7.5% for teachers, researchers, culture workers and statutory officers), an 8% rise in the minimum wage to €1,245, and a €150 million family package, offset in part by 0.5% cuts in ministries' appropriations and €197 million from stricter tax administration.
significance: First budget of the Sinkevičius government; pending in the Seimas as of October 2026. Its deficit above the 3% EU reference value has been criticised by the opposition and coalition partners.

description: A package of measures the government puts at almost €770 million: childcare and employment vouchers usable for nannies, after-school groups and camps (€61.35 million in 2027), €40 million of support for buying a home with extra incentives in the regions, €25 million for higher pension guarantees for people raising children, a €23.65 million one-off allowance for first-graders' school needs, and a planned increase in childcare benefits, which the Prime Minister says the coalition wants to bring forward from 2028 to 1 July 2027.
significance: The main demographic measure of the government programme; submitted with the 2027 budget, not yet adopted as of October 2026.

description: Approved by the government in autumn 2026: about 6,000 km of overhead power lines in wooded areas are to be replaced with underground cables by 2030, and emergency-repair capacity strengthened, to protect the grid against storms and external threats.
significance: Part of the government's resilience agenda alongside €300 million for dual-use hospital infrastructure.

law_name: Amendments to the Law on Investment and the Land Law
description: Submitted by the government and adopted by the Seimas in autumn 2026 to reduce administrative obstacles for investors, make it quicker to find suitable plots and ease large investments and job creation.
significance: Presented by the government as its main deregulation measure of its first 100 days, together with an initiative against 'gold-plating' when transposing EU law.

law_name: Temporary 50% discount on regional train and intercity bus tickets
description: In response to high fuel prices, the government applied a 50% discount on local (regional) train tickets from October to the end of 2026 and announced the same discount on long-distance bus tickets from November to the end of the year.
significance: One of the government's short-term measures against rising fuel prices, alongside €20 million of extra support for farmers.

law_name: Action plan to prevent sexual crimes and protect minors
description: Prepared on the Prime Minister's initiative: stricter liability, stronger child-protection requirements, limits on suspects' and defendants' ability to work with children, and wider specialised help and treatment to reduce reoffending.
significance: A Prime Minister's initiative announced in the government's 100-day report.

law_name: Application for full membership of CERN
description: After a decision announced on 21 August 2026, Sinkevičius sent CERN's leadership an official letter on 26 August 2026 applying for Lithuania's full membership; Lithuania has been an associate member since 2018.
significance: Implements a goal of the government programme; membership requires a decision by CERN's member states.
